About

The developer behind this page

EryyynIT is the public identity. Michael is the person. This is where they meet.

EryyynIT is the name I develop under — pronounced roughly like "Eryn", with an IT suffix, because that's the technical side of me. On a first-name basis, I'm Michael.

I build backend systems end to end. Commercially that means Python and FastAPI, with Go alongside. The rest of the time: infrastructure, small games, AI experiments, and anything that starts with an idea and ends with something that runs.

This page is my hub — the work, the game, and where I share the process. No buzzwords, no fake seniority; just what I build and how I build it.

Backend · Python

Async Payment Processing Service

Experiment

An event-driven payment microservice built with FastAPI and RabbitMQ — outbox pattern, dead letter queue, idempotency and webhook notifications. A hands-on look at reliable messaging and retry logic.

Built to get comfortable with event-driven architecture — and with what happens when a message arrives twice, out of order, or not at all.

FastAPIRabbitMQPostgreSQLDocker
View on GitHub
Backend · Go

queue

Experiment

A small in-memory queue broker written in Go, stdlib only, exposed over an HTTP API with two endpoints. Built to understand FIFO semantics and concurrency without a framework in the way.

Wanted to feel how a queue works from the inside before reaching for the big tools.

GostdlibHTTP API
